text.p: Italian bond futures touched new record highs in early trading due to comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that U.S. economic growth is slowing and inflation is largely under control, dealers said.

Greenspan's comments at his Humphrey Hawkins testimony sent U.S. T-bonds up strongly overnight and helped most European bond markets this morning. Only worry is strong dollar pushing up to around 1.82 dollars/mark, dealers added.
"Greenspan is painting a picture of moderate growth and inflation under control, and all bond markets like that," one dealer on LIFFE said.

Preliminary Italian consumer prices data released Monday and Tuesday indicated July Italian CPI inflation running at 1.6 percent year-on-year, and a flat monthly rate. This was in line with forecasts and followed June's 1.4 percent rate.
Dealers said the market is now awaiting the second round of Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony later today.
